title: finding(devx): the emit census's root bound refuses 3 of create-plugin's templates for specifiers the generator's OWN emitted package.json declares
body:
Filed by the `os-dev` implementing objectui#8139 (PM session `session_01FhBNJcLRZLe8M87VcUgpKr`, R46), as an out-of-scope observation found while measuring that card. `finding` only, left unassigned; grading and `domain:*` are the triage seat's.

Dedupe: the repo-scoped REST channel is available to this seat for issue reads but `GET /search/issues` is refused ("sessions are bound to their configured repositories"), so one targeted MCP `search_issues` was used instead — `emit census root bound refuses templates whose specifiers the generated package.json declares`, 14 results. Nearest are objectui#7472 (a different census blind spot: an emitted icon resolver invisible to the record-reading census) and objectui#8139 itself. Neither is about this.

## The reading

`scripts/check-doc-snippet-types.mjs`'s emitted-code census refuses a template when it imports a bare specifier that this repository's ROOT manifest declares and that no `paths` entry covers (`resolvesOnlyThroughRootManifest`). The rule's stated purpose is right: such a specifier reaches the snippet only through this workspace's own installation, "not through anything the emitted file's reader installs".

But for a GENERATOR, the census already knows what the reader installs — the same generator writes it. `packages/create-plugin/src/templates.ts`'s `buildPackageJson` emits a `package.json` declaring `vitest`, `@testing-library/react`, `@testing-library/jest-dom`, `vite`, `vite-plugin-dts` and the rest (`DEV_DEPENDENCIES`, templates.ts:87-96). The census does not read that emitted manifest, so on `0e49b95d8` it reports:

| site | census verdict | what the scaffolded repo actually has |
|---|---|---|
| `templates.ts:314` (`buildVitestSetup`) | `[bound]` refused on `@testing-library/jest-dom/vitest` | declared, `^7.0.1` |
| `templates.ts:491` (`buildTestFile`) | `[bound]` refused on `@testing-library/react`, `vitest` | declared, `^16.3.2` / `^4.1.10` |
| `templates.ts:270` (`buildViteConfig`) | `[semantic]` TS2307 on `vite-plugin-dts` | declared, `^5.0.3` |

So 3 of `create-plugin`'s 8 recognised templates are either never judged or judged against the wrong manifest — on the very generator whose real defect (objectui#8139's TS2769) the census found. The census's own summary is explicit that a refusal "is not a pass".

## Why it is worth recording

It is not only lost coverage, it actively pushes a fix the wrong way. objectui#8139 offered two shapes for typing the scaffolded `test:` block, and one of them — importing `defineConfig` from `vitest/config` — makes the census report ZERO diagnostics on `buildViteConfig`'s template. Measured on `b38014e82`: `Judged 12 ... 7 refused by the root bound` with the triple-slash reference, versus `Judged 11 ... 8 refused` with the import, the latter clean only because the block stopped being compiled at all. The implementer chose the reference for exactly this reason, but the next reader of that number has no way to tell a clean template from an unjudged one without opening the `[bound]` list.

## A possible direction (not a proposal, and NOT verified)

The census header already names a "declared-dependency path" — the per-package `declaredBy` map built from each workspace package's own `dependencies`. A generator's EMITTED manifest is the same kind of fact, one step further out. Whether that belongs in the bound, in the artefact classifier, or in a declared ledger is objectui#7864's decision, not this card's.

## Explicitly not claimed

I did not verify that reading the emitted manifest is mechanically feasible here (the census substitutes holes before compiling, and `buildPackageJson` returns an object, not a template literal). This card records the measurement, not the remedy.

## Back-links

objectui#8139 (the card that surfaced it, and where the TS2307 row was first recorded as an instrument artefact), objectui#7864 / PR #8138 (the census), objectui#7472 (the other open census blind spot).
